data.name: cipw_overview
data.value: The CIPW norm calculation (also called CIPW Norm) is a petrochemical method proposed by Cross, Iddings, Pirsson and Washington in 1902. Based on whole-rock major-element oxide analyses, it allocates oxides to a set of idealized standard minerals in a fixed priority order, supporting rock classification and comparative studies.

data.name: cipw_step1_detail
data.value: • Normalize input major-element oxides on an anhydrous basis (to 100%) • Partition iron: split FeOT into FeO and Fe₂O₃ using the user-defined Fe³⁺/Fe ratio • Combine MnO into FeO based on molar ratio • Convert oxide mass percentages to moles

data.name: cipw_step2_detail
data.value: Consume volatile components in priority order to form: • Calcite (Cc): CO₂ + CaO • Fluorite (Fl): F + CaO • Pyrite (Py): S + FeO • Halite (Hl): Cl + Na₂O • Mirabilite (Th): SO₃ + Na₂O

data.name: cipw_step3_detail
data.value: Allocate trace components to accessory minerals: • Zircon (Z): ZrO₂ + SiO₂ • Apatite (Ap): P₂O₅ + CaO • Chromite (Cm): Cr₂O₃ + FeO • Ilmenite (Ilm): TiO₂ + FeO (Titanite and rutile are formed after anorthite; see the feldspar step.)

data.name: cipw_step4_detail
data.value: Determine the alumina saturation type from the molar ratio between residual Al₂O₃ and alkalis + CaO: • Peralkaline: Na₂O + K₂O > Al₂O₃ • Metaluminous: Al₂O₃ ≤ CaO + Na₂O + K₂O • Peraluminous: Al₂O₃ > CaO + Na₂O + K₂O

data.name: cipw_step5_detail
data.value: Allocate alkalis and alumina to feldspars in turn: • Orthoclase (Or): K₂O + Al₂O₃ + 6SiO₂ • Albite (Ab): Na₂O + Al₂O₃ + 6SiO₂ • Anorthite (An): CaO + Al₂O₃ + 2SiO₂ • Titanite (Tn): TiO₂ + CaO + SiO₂ (uses only the CaO left after anorthite) • Rutile (Ru): residual TiO₂ • Corundum (Cor): residual Al₂O₃ (peraluminous case) • Acmite (Ac): Na₂O + Fe₂O₃ + 4SiO₂ (peralkaline case) • Residual alkali silicates (ns, ks)

data.name: cipw_step6_detail
data.value: Allocate iron oxides to minerals: • Magnetite (Mt): Fe₂O₃ + FeO • Hematite (Hm): residual Fe₂O₃

data.name: cipw_step7_detail
data.value: Distribute remaining MgO, FeO and CaO to ferromagnesian silicates: • Diopside (Di): CaO + MgO + 2SiO₂ (Mg end-member) • Hedenbergite (Hd): CaO + FeO + 2SiO₂ (Fe end-member) • Enstatite (En): MgO + SiO₂ • Ferrosilite (Fs): FeO + SiO₂ • Wollastonite (Wo): residual CaO + SiO₂

data.name: cipw_step8_detail
data.value:
Adjust according to the SiO₂ residual:
▶ Oversaturated (SiO₂ left over): form quartz (Q) ▶ Saturated (SiO₂ exactly used): no quartz, no feldspathoids ▶ Undersaturated (SiO₂ deficient): convert minerals in priority order— • Hypersthene (En+Fs) → Olivine (Fo+Fa) • Titanite (Tn) → Perovskite (Pf) • Albite (Ab) → Nepheline (Ne) • Orthoclase (Or) → Leucite (Le) • Wollastonite (Wo) → Larnite (Cs) • Diopside/Hedenbergite (Di+Hd) → Larnite (Cs) + Olivine (Fo+Fa) • Leucite (Le) → Pseudoleucite (Kp)

data.name: cipw_step9_detail
data.value: • Multiply each mineral mole count by its molar mass to obtain its standard mineral mass • Normalize to mass percentages (wt%) for output • Report silica saturation, alumina saturation state and mass-balance error diagnostics

data.name: cipw_references_content
data.value: • Cross, W., Iddings, J.P., Pirsson, L.V., Washington, H.S. (1902). A Quantitative Chemico-Mineralogical Classification and Nomenclature of Igneous Rocks. • Le Maitre, R.W. (2002). Igneous Rocks: A Classification and Glossary of Terms. Cambridge University Press. • Kelsey, C.H. (1965). Calculation of the CIPW norm. Mineralogical Magazine, 34, 276-282.

data.name: niggli_help_overview
data.value: The Barth-Niggli molecular norm (Catanorm) was proposed by the Swiss petrologists Paul Niggli (1948) and Tom F. W. Barth (1948). Unlike the traditional CIPW norm, which uses weight percentages, the Niggli system uses cation-equivalent percentages. This removes the bias that heavy elements such as Fe introduce into volume proportions, so the result lies closer to the modal mineral volume percentages seen in thin section. This module also calculates the classical Niggli numbers (si, al, fm, c, alk, k, mg, qz).

data.name: niggli_references_gcdkit

data.name: niggli_step1_detail
data.value: Oxide weight percentages are divided by molar mass and multiplied by cation counts to obtain millications. The sum of all cations is normalized to 100%. Total iron (FeOT) can be partitioned using the adjustable Fe3+/Fe ratio (default 0.15).

data.name: niggli_step1_hy_ol_done
data.value: Desilication Step 1: Orthopyroxene -> Olivine (Hy → Ol), consumed {0}% Hy, silica deficit completely eliminated

data.name: niggli_step1_hy_ol_part
data.value: Desilication Step 1: Orthopyroxene -> Olivine (Hy → Ol), all Hy ({0}%) converted to Ol, remaining deficit D = {1}%

data.name: niggli_step2_detail
data.value: From the molecular proportions set base = al + fm + c + alk = 100, and calculate si, al, fm, c, alk, ti and p, together with k = K2O/(Na2O+K2O) and mg = MgO/(FeO+2Fe2O3+MnO+MgO). The quartz index qz = si - (100 + 4*al) shows the silica saturation of the rock directly.

data.name: niggli_step2_tn_pf_done
data.value: Desilication Step 2: Titanite -> Perovskite (Tn → Pf), consumed {0}% Tn, silica deficit completely eliminated

data.name: niggli_step2_tn_pf_part
data.value: Desilication Step 2: Titanite -> Perovskite (Tn → Pf), all Tn converted, remaining deficit D = {0}%

data.name: niggli_step3_ab_ne_done
data.value: Desilication Step 3: Albite -> Nepheline (Ab → Ne), consumed {0}% Ab, silica deficit completely eliminated

data.name: niggli_step3_ab_ne_part
data.value: Desilication Step 3: Albite -> Nepheline (Ab → Ne), all Ab converted, remaining deficit D = {0}%

data.name: niggli_step3_detail
data.value: Early allocation: CO2 and Ca form Calcite (Cc); P, F and Ca form Apatite (Ap); remaining F forms Fluorite (Fr); S and Fe2+ form Pyrite (Py); Ti and Fe2+ form Ilmenite (Il).

data.name: niggli_step4_detail
data.value: K forms Orthoclase (Or) and Potassium Metasilicate (Ks). Na forms Albite (Ab), Acmite (Ac), and Sodium Metasilicate (Ns). Remaining Al forms Anorthite (An) and Corundum (C). Ti forms Titanite (Tn) or Rutile (Ru).

data.name: niggli_step4_or_lc_done
data.value: Desilication Step 4: Orthoclase -> Leucite (Or → Lc), consumed {0}% Or, silica deficit completely eliminated

data.name: niggli_step4_or_lc_part
data.value: Desilication Step 4: Orthoclase -> Leucite (Or → Lc), all Or converted, remaining deficit D = {0}%

data.name: niggli_step4_title
data.value: Alkali feldspars, anorthite, and peralkaline minerals

data.name: niggli_step5_detail
data.value: Fe3+ and Fe2+ form Magnetite (Mt) and Hematite (Hm). Ca, Mg, and Fe2+ form Wollastonite (Wo), Enstatite (En), and Ferrosilite (Fs). En + Fs form Orthopyroxene (Hy). Wo and Hy combine to form Diopside (Di).

data.name: niggli_step5_lc_kp_done
data.value: Desilication Step 5: Leucite -> Kalsilite (Lc → Kp), consumed {0}% Lc, silica deficit completely eliminated

data.name: niggli_step5_lc_kp_part
data.value: Desilication Step 5: Leucite -> Kalsilite (Lc → Kp), all Lc converted, remaining deficit D = {0}%

data.name: niggli_step5_title
data.value: Allocation of iron oxides and pyroxenes

data.name: niggli_step6_detail
data.value: If residual Si >= 0, quartz (Q) forms. If Si < 0, the silica deficit is D = -Si and desilication follows thermodynamic stability: ① Hy → Ol (4 Hy become 3 Ol and release 1 Si) ② Tn → Pf (3 Tn become 2 Pf and release 1 Si) ③ Ab → Ne (5 Ab become 3 Ne and release 2 Si) ④ Or → Lc (5 Or become 4 Lc and release 1 Si) ⑤ Lc → Kp (4 Lc become 3 Kp and release 1 Si) ⑥ Wo → Cs (4 Wo become 3 Cs and release 1 Si) ⑦ Di → Cs + Ol (4 Di become 1.5 Cs + 1.5 Ol and release 1 Si).

data.name: niggli_step6_wo_cs_done
data.value: Desilication Step 6: Wollastonite -> Rankinite (Wo → Cs), consumed {0}% Wo, silica deficit completely eliminated

data.name: niggli_step6_wo_cs_part
data.value: Desilication Step 6: Wollastonite -> Rankinite (Wo → Cs), all Wo converted, remaining deficit D = {0}%

data.name: niggli_step7_di_cs_ol_done
data.value: Desilication Step 7: Diopside -> Rankinite + Olivine (Di → Cs + Ol), consumed {0}% Di, silica deficit completely eliminated

data.name: niggli_step7_di_cs_ol_part
